author: Dewey Sim
description:
When China and the United States agreed in May to frame their relationship as a “constructive relationship of strategic stability”, the phrase left many observers trying to guess what it actually meant.
Four months on, they have added an elaboration that offers further insight into the two sides’ respective priorities.
After presidents Xi Jinping and Donald Trump met in Washington last month, the two sides pledged to build a “constructive relationship of strategic stability on the basis of...
title: What are the concerns and priorities behind the new language used to define China-US ties?

author: Nayan Seth
description:
The Port of Los Angeles, the largest container port in the United States and the country’s leading gateway for imports from China and other Asian countries, had its busiest three-month period on record from July through to September, despite persistent uncertainty over tariffs and shifting global trade supply chains.
“If there was ever a time for a drum roll, this is it,” said Gene Seroka, executive director of the Port of Los Angeles, during a media briefing on Friday.
“July through September...
title: Key US port for China imports records best-ever quarter despite trade uncertainty

author: Zhang Tong
description:
US President Donald Trump has opened the American market to Russian diesel, reversing years of sanctions pressure on Moscow just three weeks after signing a law to punish buyers of its energy, as record fuel prices threaten his party in next month’s midterm elections.
Trump said on Truth Social on Friday that he and Russian President Vladimir Putin had reached the supply deal in a phone call that had been expected to focus on suspected plague cases in Russia.
According to Trump, Russia will...
title: Trump announces major diesel deal with Russia ahead of US midterm elections next month

author: Cao Jiaxuan
description:
China’s cooperation with the Pacific islands is not part of a geopolitical competition, top diplomat Wang Yi told a delegation of politicians from the region on Friday.
The comments come as Beijing and Washington vie for influence in the South Pacific.
“China’s engagement with Pacific island countries is a form of South-South cooperation based on mutual assistance and support,” Wang said, according to a statement from the Communist Party’s International Department.
“This cooperation does not...
title: China’s Pacific ties not part of ‘geopolitical rivalry’, Wang Yi tells island leaders

author: Orange Wang
description:
China should avoid taking a “confrontational posture” over a new security pact between the United States, Denmark and Greenland as it might end up being excluded from engagement on the emerging Arctic order.
That was the warning from Shanghai Jiao Tong University’s National Institute of Strategic Studies (NISS), a Chinese think tank, in a report released on Wednesday.
It also said the US was unlikely to turn the northern polar region into its “exclusive strategic backyard”. The report noted that...
title: Why a ‘confrontational posture’ won’t help China in the Arctic

author: Liu Zhen
description:
Polar researchers have used a would-be Chinese rival to Elon Musk’s Starlink to make a satellite video call between the Arctic and Antarctic – the first publicly reported test of the Guowang constellation.
The call highlights the growing capabilities of the country’s satellite constellations, according to state media.
Beijing has been accelerating the development of its low-Earth-orbit constellations in recent years, particularly as the US-based Starlink showed its wartime value by helping...
title: Chinese researchers make Arctic-to-Antarctic call using rival to Musk’s Starlink

author: Finbarr Bermingham,Dewey Sim,Xiaofei Xu
description:
The European Union and China “reached an understanding” on trade in hybrid electric vehicles during marathon negotiations in Beijing on Friday, China’s commerce ministry said in a statement.
Beijing is “willing to continue” fast-tracking licenses for rare earth mineral exports to Europe, while the sides will continue negotiations on reducing tariffs and creating minimum price deals that would allow Chinese electric vehicles to enter the EU market at a lower duty rate, according to the...
title: China and EU reach ‘understanding’ on hybrid vehicles after crunch trade talks

author: Raymond Ma,Neil Denslow
description:
China’s central bank rejected claims that the yuan is undervalued, rebutting a key European argument amid crunch negotiations ahead of a possible trade war.
“China has no need or intent to gain competitive advantages through currency devaluation, nor has it ever resorted to competitive devaluation,” the People’s Bank of China said in a policy paper on Thursday, printed in both Chinese and English (see the full paper on SCMP Plus). “China’s trade growth is driven by its growing industrial...
title: China rejects yuan complaints, ‘golden week’ travel, Canton Fair

author: Victoria Bela
description:
While Russian authorities have denied the death of a woman who worked in a laboratory at an anti-plague institute in Siberia was connected with the pathogen, the incident has sparked global concern – including in China – over a potential spread of the disease and a lack of transparency.
US President Donald Trump said on Tuesday that he planned to speak with his Russian counterpart Vladimir Putin after it emerged late last week that the 28-year-old female lab technician had been admitted to...
title: Russia lifts plague lab-related measures. Should China – and the world – be relieved?

author: Shi Jiangtao
description:
China and the Philippines have traded accusations over a medical evacuation near the disputed Second Thomas Shoal, as Manila reports a near-doubling of Chinese military and coastguard vessels around contested South China Sea features in September.
The latest exchange centred on the evacuation on Thursday of an injured Filipino serviceman from the BRP Sierra Madre, a Philippine naval vessel grounded on Second Thomas Shoal decades ago.
Known as Renai Jiao in China and Ayungin Shoal in the...
title: China and Philippines blame each other over South China Sea medical mission

author: William Zheng,Khushboo Razdan
description:
US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent may skip a meeting of Apec finance ministers in Hong Kong later this month to focus on preparing for President Donald Trump’s historic visit to Shenzhen in November, sources told the South China Morning Post.
Bessent is expected to meet Chinese Vice-Premier He Lifeng in Shenzhen ahead of Trump’s visit – when Trump will again hold talks with President Xi Jinping – as the two sides look to secure a longer extension of the bilateral trade truce, which is due to...
title: Bessent may skip Apec in Hong Kong to focus on Trump’s Shenzhen visit, sources say

author: Junjie Wang
description:
Chinese President Xi Jinping was busy travelling abroad last month. In September, he paid a historic state visit to the United States, his first to the country in more than a decade. He also made his first visit to India in seven years, meeting Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi on the sidelines of the Brics summit.
China will host the annual Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation summit in November, where Xi will meet US President Donald Trump for the third time this year. During the summit, Xi is...
title: Xi Jinping meets foreign leaders: tracker, September 2026

author: Eve Qiao
description:
A rare work of Chinese calligraphy long presumed destroyed in the chaos of 1945 only to resurface 81 years later, fetched HK$177.45 million (US$22.6 million) in Hong Kong on Wednesday.
The work called Jishi Tie, or Accumulated Time Letter, by early Tang dynasty (618-907) calligrapher Yu Shinan, went under the hammer at China Guardian Hong Kong’s autumn auction at the Hong Kong Convention and Exhibition Centre.
It fetched HK$155 million at the hammer, with the final price including the buyer’s...
title: Rare Chinese calligraphy scroll resurfaces after 81 years, sells for US$22.6 million

author: Gabriel Dominguez
description:
China is running the most systematic effort of any outside power to learn from the drone war in Ukraine, with military and defence-industry analysts typically writing up new battlefield techniques within about four months, according to a new analysis.
But it usually took a year or more before those lessons showed up publicly in People’s Liberation Army (PLA) training, equipment or force structure, Lilly Min-Chen Lee and Kateryna Bondar wrote in a commentary published on October 7 by the...
title: How quickly is China learning from the Ukraine war’s latest drone tactics?
